title: The story of jeans
text:
Jeans are so common today that it is hard to imagine a time without them. Their story starts in the 1870s in Nevada, with a tailor named Jacob Davis {A}. His customers complained that the pockets of their work trousers kept tearing under the weight of tools and stones, so Davis fixed small metal rivets to the pockets {B}.

He knew that his invention could easily be copied, but he could not afford the patent fee, so he wrote to his supplier of cloth, Levi Strauss, {C}. The two men took out a joint patent, and the first 'blue jeans' were produced. For decades they were worn almost only by workers: farmers, cowboys and railway builders.

Everything changed in the 1950s, when film stars such as James Dean wore jeans on screen. Teenagers saw them as a sign of freedom, {D}, and some schools and cinemas even banned them. Parents were not amused, but the fashion could not be stopped.

Today the average person owns several pairs, and manufacturers produce billions each year. The process uses enormous amounts of water, {E}, so some companies have started to recycle old jeans into new fibres. Whatever happens, {F}.
